title: Nasdaq surges 7% as the AI trade roars back after Jensen Huang is reinstated as Nvidia CEO
excerpt: The Dow soared more than 1,400 points and the Nasdaq surged 7% as Jensen Huang was brought back as Nvidia CEO.
content_html:
By Jennifer Sor

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-23T16:00:47.684Z

Jensen Huang is back and the stock market couldn't be happier.

AI stocks are in the midst of a sharp rebound as traders raced to buy Friday's dip and took in news that Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO, removing a huge overhang that pummeled the AI trade last week.

The news caps off a wild, weekslong saga that began with reports of Huang having an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led investors to dump Nvidia and the data center suppliers in its orbit.

In a statement, the board said it believed Huang was the "right person to lead Nvidia," and that it took input from US government officials, which led it to be confident that Huang would pose no national security risk on the company. In a separate statement, Huang said he was "honored" to come back.

Shares of Nvidia soared 34% on Monday as investors took in his reinstatement. The stock had plunged as much as 47% from its latest peak, and was down 21% last week.

Glen Smith, the chief investment officer at GDS Wealth Management, called the decision to reinstate Huang "shocking."

"Nvidia's stock is understandably surging on the news to reinstate Jensen Huang because much of its decline stemmed from this Nvidia crisis and it appears that the worst is over," he wrote in a note.

AI stocks took it on the chin when Huang was first ousted. The Nvidia founder is seen as an unofficial poster child for the AI trade, leading his departure to be viewed in an existential light.

The tech sector was up across the board. The iShares Semiconductor ETF surged more than 13%, while the Roundhill Neocloud ETF soared 20%.

Here's where US indexes stood around 11 a.m. ET on Monday:

  • S&P 500: 7,256.49, up 5.01%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 49,669.61, up 3.16% (+1,522.28 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 26,768.96, up 6.95%

Investors had been rooting for Huang to make a comeback as he was ousted from Nvidia, though the return, until Monday, looked unlikely. Nvidia's board said they were not considering bringing back Huang on the company's third-quarter earnings call, the first where Huang was absent.

The rebound has provided the AI sector some much-needed stability after last week's bruising sell-off, with the S&P 500 logging its worst losing streak in years as the tech sell-off accelerated.

The Nasdaq 100 remains deep in correction territory. The benchmark index teetered on the edge of a bear market on Friday, is 14% lower from its latest peak.

Monday's rally has market pros wondering whether the move is a dead-cat bounce, a short-lived recovery in asset prices before the sell-off ultimately continues. The surge in stock prices appears partly fueled by the holiday-shortened trading week, which lowers trading volume and stokes volatility, top economist David Rosenberg wrote in a client note.

"We are seeing a classic dead cat bounce in US futures in the wake of last week's epic drubbing," Rosenberg said on Monday. "Equities are definitely oversold, and remember that the best days the stock market has ever enjoyed happened in bear phases," he added.

"As we get closer to Thanksgiving this week, more people will be hitting the roads or the skies, so expect exaggerated moves in both directions," Paul Hickey, the co-founder of Bespoke Investment Group, wrote in a note.

Concerns are also swirling around the strength of the US economy and the prospect of higher interest rates in 2027, particularly as central bankers signal a hawkish bias heading into their December policy meeting. Strategists on JPMorgan's markets intelligence team noted that recession fears were on the rise, as evidenced by the outperformance of the bank's Recession stock basket.

Investors are also waiting on fresh personal consumption expenditures data, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, on Wednesday, it noted.

The "question is whether this is a deadcat bounce or the start of a more sustainable rally into year-end," JPMorgan said. The bank recently raised its year-end price target for the S&P 500 to 8,000, implying 15% upside from Friday's levels.

Wednesday's PCE data will likely serve as a "final major test" for markets ahead of the Fed's meeting, Lukman Otunuga, the head of market research at FXTM, wrote in a note.

"With markets already pricing in a December hike, a hot print could add fuel to the fire, and with Thanksgiving thinning out liquidity, even small surprises could spark outsized moves," he wrote.

The stock market has been rattled by back-to-back fears about AI, with investors panicking about a possible slowdown in AI capex and data center construction in recent weeks. Huang's resignation and reports of his alleged affairs further destabilized the trade in November.

Monday's rally has market pros wondering whether the move is a dead-cat bounce, a short-lived recovery in asset prices before the sell-off ultimately continues. The surge in stock prices appears partly fueled by the holiday-shortened trading week, which lowers trading volume and stokes volatility, top economist David Rosenberg wrote in a client note.

"We are seeing a classic dead cat bounce in US futures in the wake of last week's epic drubbing," Rosenberg said on Monday. "Equities are definitely oversold, and remember that the best days the stock market has ever enjoyed happened in bear phases," he added.

"As we get closer to Thanksgiving this week, more people will be hitting the roads or the skies, so expect exaggerated moves in both directions," Paul Hickey, the co-founder of Bespoke Investment Group, wrote in a note.

Concerns are also swirling around the strength of the US economy and the prospect of higher interest rates in 2027, particularly as central bankers signal a hawkish bias heading into their December policy meeting. Strategists on JPMorgan's markets intelligence team noted that recession fears were on the rise, as evidenced by the outperformance of the bank's Recession stock basket.

Investors are also waiting on fresh personal consumption expenditures data, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, on Wednesday, it noted.

The "question is whether this is a deadcat bounce or the start of a more sustainable rally into year-end," JPMorgan said. The bank recently raised its year-end price target for the S&P 500 to 8,000, implying 15% upside from Friday's levels.

Wednesday's PCE data will likely serve as a "final major test" for markets ahead of the Fed's meeting, Lukman Otunuga, the head of market research at FXTM, wrote in a note.

"With markets already pricing in a December hike, a hot print could add fuel to the fire, and with Thanksgiving thinning out liquidity, even small surprises could spark outsized moves," he wrote.

The stock market has been rattled by back-to-back fears about AI, with investors panicking about a possible slowdown in AI capex and data center construction in recent weeks. Huang's resignation and reports of his alleged affairs further destabilized the trade in November.
